CHROMIUM: virtwl: Kick the in virtqueue in virtwl_vfd_remove() virtwl_vfd_remove() returns any in-queue buffers owned by the vfd to the device, but doesn't kick the virtqueue. This works out as long as the in-queue isn't completely full, because the next thing to be written to it will trigger a queue kick, but if the queue is completely blocked the system does not recover. Auto-include Kconfig headers The CONFIG/IS_ENABLED macros will assume that any option which is not defined is 0 (disabled). This is dangerous for typos (which this patch can't help) and also dangerous because if you forget to include <config.h> all depthcharge Kconfigs will be considered disabled. Let's switch the depthcharge build system to include Kconfig headers automatically (like coreboot has already been doing for a long time) to at least prevent the second kind of mistakes. Also added a fix to make sure $(src) and $(obj) are absolute paths even if they're passed in on the command line. This is important when passing them to the subinvocation of $(MAKE) for vboot. llvm: add llvm-next_pgo_use; change our profile naming scheme This CL adds a llvm-next-specific pgo_use flag, and changes our profile naming scheme slightly. Digests have been updated appropriately. The intent behind tweaking our naming scheme is 'free' uprevving for our profiles. Since profiles are pinned to the SHA of LLVM's HEAD, the failure mode for PGO shifts from "oh, we've forgotten to update these over the last N rolls and our perf is silently degraded," to "oh, `emerge llvm` fails this change forgot to handle our PGO bits." These failures of `emerge llvm` should only happen when someone's trying to update LLVM's HEAD SHA. Moving it forward in time without a corresponding PGO profile will break the build if PGO for the LLVM we're updating has PGO on by default. To reiterate, AIUI, our intent for rolling PGO with LLVM is as follows: 1. We disable llvm-next_pgo_use by default, and roll llvm-next to a new base revision. 2. We vet the base revision, apply patches, etc. 3. Once we're happy with the stability of this base revision, we run the merging script in toolchain-utils to generate a profile for the new base revision. 4. Some time later, llvm-next becomes llvm The intent is for llvm_pgo_use to "always" be on, so there are two kinds of updates that can break `emerge llvm` (again, super early in the build). Either: - we're updating llvm-next to a new revision, and forget to turn llvm-next_pgo_use off by default (trivial fix), or - we're updating llvm to llvm-next, and forgot to generate a PGO profile for llvm-next. This can be fixed by generating that PGO profile, doing whatever additional vetting that we want for this PGO'ed llvm-next, and then actually rolling llvm to llvm-next. Both of these seem acceptable, and preferable to allowing a stale profile to slowly stagnate to me. Other opinions are welcome. :) This will require an update to our upload-pgo script in toolchain-utils; that'll be added shortly. BUG=None TEST=`emerge llvm && USE=llvm-next emerge llvm`, with varying values for llvm_pgo_use and llvm-next_pgo_use. llvm and llvm-next both pulled their profiles when their respective _pgo_use options were enabled. FROMGIT: ASoC: core: use component driver name as component name fmt_single_name() uses device name to determine component name. If multiple components bind to the same device, the debugfs creation in soc_init_component_debugfs() would fail due to duplicated entity names. Name provided by component driver is unique enough to represent each component. Use component driver name as the component name to avoid name duplication. power: set_wifi_transmit_power: refactor device, driver detection Fix a number of TODO issues, to prepare for adding 1 more driver. * Device detection: rather than hardcode wlan0 and mlan0, just search /sys/class/net/* looking for device(s) with a 'DEVTYPE=wlan' uevent property. - With this, we technically might see more than 1 WiFi device -- if, for example, a user plugs in a USB WiFi dongle. Support this by enumerating all WiFi devices, and seeing if we have supported methods for any of them. * Driver detection: rather than assume based on the presence of /sys/module/ paths (b/c multiple drivers can be loaded, even if they're not all in use), look up the driver for a given device via its .../device/driver symlink. This is what we do for device/driver validation in Autotest as well.
